title: Bengaluru Court Bars Way2News From Using AppsForBharat's Confidential Data
excerpt: A Bengaluru court's interim order pits two funded startups — AppsForBharat's Sri Mandir and Way2News's Veda Mandir — against each other over confidential data allegedly carried out the door by a former employee. Way2News denies everything.
body:
• A Bengaluru commercial court passed an ad-interim ex parte injunction on September 10 restraining Way2News from using AppsForBharat's confidential information and intellectual property allegedly obtained from a former employee.
  • AppsForBharat, which operates the Sri Mandir devotional app, alleges former senior operations associate Shivam Kumar Singh joined Way2News in violation of a non-compete clause and shared proprietary data with rival platform Veda Mandir.
  • Way2News denies the allegations, telling Entrackr the Google Drive access was an inadvertent click on an old link and that it has not received any court order so far.
  • The next hearing is listed for October 5, 2026 — the date that will likely determine whether the interim restraint holds once both sides are heard.

A Bengaluru commercial court has temporarily restrained hyperlocal news startup Way2News from using confidential information and intellectual property belonging to AppsForBharat, the operator of the spiritual tech platform Sri Mandir. The ad-interim ex parte injunction was passed on Thursday, September 10, in a commercial suit filed by AppsForBharat against Way2News and its former employee Shivam Kumar Singh.

The order restrains Way2News, its directors, employees, agents, and others acting on its behalf from using AppsForBharat's confidential information, intellectual property, and other data allegedly received from Singh until the next hearing. Because the order was passed ex parte, Way2News and Singh were not heard before the interim relief was granted.

What AppsForBharat alleges

According to court filings accessed by Inc42, Singh worked as a senior operations associate at AppsForBharat, where he coordinated with priests and temples and managed on-ground pooja operations. He resigned on August 3, 2026, citing "personal exigencies," with his last working day on August 7.

https://x.com/upadhyay_harsh1/status/2098676122527683031

AppsForBharat alleged that one of its employees received a request from Singh on August 25 seeking access to the startup's Google Drive — a request sent using a Way2News email address, which prompted an internal investigation. The startup claimed the drive contained videos, marketing material, operational information, financial data, and details of suppliers and customers.

AppsForBharat further alleged that Singh joined Way2News in violation of the non-compete provision in his employment agreement and shared its confidential information with the platform. It also accused Way2News's spiritual tech platform Veda Mandir of publishing promotional videos identical to marketing material created by Sri Mandir. AppsForBharat sought ₹1 crore in damages for alleged losses and contractual breaches, the return of its confidential material, permanent injunctions, and an account of revenue generated through its alleged unauthorized use.

Way2News's response

Way2News denies the allegations. In a statement to Entrackr, which first reported the order, the company gave a different account of the Drive access: the link was old and tied to Singh's previous job. Singh "inadvertently accessed the link," the company said, then realized he was still in legacy WhatsApp groups from his old workplace and left them. There was, it said, "no intent to obtain, transfer or use" anything.

"No intent to obtain, transfer or use."

— Way2News, in a statement to Entrackr, on the former employee's access to AppsForBharat's Google Drive

The company also told Entrackr that it had not received any court order so far — a live procedural point, since service of the order remains in question. AppsForBharat had additionally sought ex parte injunctions against Way2News allegedly soliciting its employees and customers, but the court declined to grant those two injunctions without hearing the defendants and issued notices instead. The current injunction is limited to the alleged use of confidential information, and does not constitute a final finding of data theft or copyright infringement.

Two funded players in a booming faith-tech market

The dispute pits two well-funded startups against each other in India's fast-growing spiritual tech market. Founded in 2020 by Prashant Sachan, AppsForBharat's Sri Mandir app lets users book online pujas and offerings, receive prasad, and access devotional content. The company raised ₹175 crore in a Series C round led by Susquehanna Asia VC in July 2025 and has raised about $65 million to date. It reports roughly 120,000 paying users and 3.5 million monthly active users.

Way2News, founded in 2015 by Raju Vanapala, began as a short-format hyperlocal news app in vernacular languages — growing out of Way2SMS — and later entered spiritual tech with Veda Mandir, which facilitates pooja, chadhava, and daan offerings at temples. The startup raised $14 million in a WestBridge Capital-led Series B round in 2024 and has raised nearly $30 million to date.

The money flowing into faith-tech is real: InstaAstro raised a Series A in August 2026, and AstroTalk reported FY25 revenue of ₹1,214.5 crore, up 85.2 percent. Devotional and astrology apps are pulling in serious capital — and this case shows the other side of that growth, where products, talent, and data move fast between rivals.

What's next

The case was heard by the LXXXVII Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge in Bengaluru, and the next hearing is listed for October 5, 2026. As legal observers have noted, an ad-interim ex parte order is a first-stage measure, not a verdict — comparable interim orders in cases like Mu Sigma in 2019 and Tremco in April 2026 collapsed once the defendant was heard. Whether this injunction survives will likely turn on whether AppsForBharat can pin down exactly what was taken, and on how Way2News's account of an inadvertent click holds up once the defense gets its turn.
